items.title: FreeRDP 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via NTLM MIC Offset
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-111880, Summary: FreeRDP versions from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contain a heap out-of-bounds write in the server hash-callback NTLM path that fails to validate the MIC offset. Unauthenticated attackers can send a crafted AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with a backward session-key offset and MIC offset to write 16 zero bytes beyond the allocation.

items.title: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
items.summary: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and NetScaler Gateway. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 according to NVD and a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.5 according to the Citrix security bulletin CTX697096. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on affected appliances. Exploitation requires no optional features to be enabled. Citrix confirmed exploitation on unmitigated appliances, and the US’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-88771 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation worldwide. Citrix has since disclosed another critical vulnerability affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, CVE-2026-107406, which can lead to RCE or denial of service. CVE-2026-107406 affects appliances configured as SAML service provider or identity provider depending on the software version. The analysis in this blog focuses on the exploitation of CVE-2026-88771.

items.title: FreeRDP 3.14.1 before 3.32.0 Integer Underflow in BMP Writer via Clipboard
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 7.2, CVEs: CVE-2026-111881, Summary: FreeRDP from 3.14.1 before 3.32.0 contains an integer underflow in the WinPR BMP writer, where a mismatched stride calculation passes SIZE_MAX - 3 to Stream_Zero for sub-byte images. A malicious RDP clipboard peer can return a crafted 1-bpp BMP processed by clipboard_synthesize_image_format_to_bmp for CF_DIB/CF_DIBV5, crashing the client or causing an out-of-bounds write.

items.title: Cybercrims go beyond stealing data to attack physical building systems
items.summary: Late Sunday night, a still-unknown cybercriminal or group hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of French grocery stores, spiking temperatures, spoiling food, and sparking fires. This is part of an ongoing trend of attacking physical systems that can do damage in the real world. In August, a ransomware attack disrupted building-management systems at a Canadian hospital, affecting door access controls, central HVAC monitoring, and the issuing of staff access cards. And three years ago, cyberattacks hit Las Vegas casinos, causing slot machines to go dark, preventing payment kiosks and ATMs from spitting out cash, and locking guests out of their rooms when the electronic keys stopped working. Not all digital intrusions remain in cyberspace, and attackers don’t need to encrypt files and steal data to cause chaos. Hitting physical systems often produces more severe consequences - and turns up the heat on executives to pay an extortion demand.

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support  - BT26-05
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: 9.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-102764, Summary: BeyondTrust has remediated a critical vulnerability in Remote Support (RS) that could allow a remote attacker to perform file operations on an affected appliance. The vulnerability exists within internal components of Remote Support. The components did not adequately validate the origin of the messages it received. Under the right conditions, this could be used to perform file operations on the appliance.

items.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.summary: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.

items.title: MALFEX npm Package 'imgdecode' Hides Shellcode Loader in Windows Native Addon
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a malicious npm package that's part of a recently disclosed software supply chain attack campaign dubbed MALFEX. The package, named "imgdecode," was uploaded to the package registry on September 30, 2026, by a user named "malfexteste8." It has been downloaded 979 times as of writing and is still available on npm as of writing. The latest version of the package is 1.0.3. "The npm package imgdecode hides a malicious loader in a compiled Node.js addon," SafeDep said. "Its nine-line JavaScript file loads a Windows dynamic-link library (DLL). When a Node.js program calls require('imgdecode') from a Windows console, the DLL attempts to download encrypted shellcode from GitHub. It decrypts the response and injects the result into a new dllhost.exe process."

items.title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
items.summary: ConnectWise has shut down customer access to its Cloud Backup service (formerly SkyKick Cloud Backup) after hackers accessed application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants. Reports of the malicious activity began emerging on Friday, with administrators observing unauthorized access to client data in Microsoft 365 tenants due to a potential “SkyKick/CW breach.” Later on the same day, managed cybersecurity and threat detection platform Huntress confirmed the worries, saying that it had identified at least 162 compromised tenants in its environment. In a post today, Microsoft also confirmed malicious activity involving ConnectWise’s Cloud Backup service, saying it identified unauthorized authentication attempts from an IP address on October 15. ConnectWise’s cloud backup solutions provide backup and recovery services that help managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams protect and restore customer data, such as emails and files, in cloud environments including Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
